scope: Independent static review of five frozen Bitcoin Motoko module optimization diffs; production and candidate source unchanged.

checks.details: Every replaced value is already Nat32 or Nat64. Byte masks and shifts preserve all bits, including maximal values and SINGLE sentinel outputs. CompactSize and bounded Nat input-index encoders retain their previous implementation.

Reader.le call graph only supplies widths 1, 2, 4, or 8; the maximum shift evaluated is 56. Bounds are checked before indexing. Input/output/witness preallocations are bounded by remaining byte counts, and all slots are populated before conversion to immutable arrays. Truncation, canonical CompactSize, trailing-data, and witness checks are preserved.
The lazy bitmap changes allocation only. Opcode parsing still covers the complete script before the zero-separator fast path; malformed pushes still reject and pushed 0xab bytes remain intact.

TapLeaf allocates exactly 64 tag bytes plus leaf version, CompactSize, and script. TapBranch allocates exactly 64 tag bytes plus two ordered 32-byte children. Hash, Address, Bip32, and Script loop offsets cover the same immutable source ranges as the former iterators.

Leading m/M roots and empty/trailing segments preserve behavior. Counting ASCII slash bytes first retains maximumDepth precedence. UTF-8 continuation bytes cannot masquerade as ASCII slash or digits. The scanner rejects the first non-ASCII byte at the same segment position as the previous character parser; numeric hardenedChild rejection still precedes later invalid characters.

independent_oracles.method: Python standard-library hashlib and integer little-endian encodings; checks source constants and arithmetic equivalence, not a replacement for Motoko execution tests.
independent_oracles.integer_cases: Zero, one, maximum, all power-of-two boundaries and adjacent values, plus 10000 seeded random values per width.
